projectSummary: Within-participant acute surface-EMG comparison of nine chest exercises in 14 resistance-trained men, with every exercise normalised to the barbell bench press rather than to a maximal voluntary contraction. MSc thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse; grey literature, not peer-reviewed.

publication.statusSource: Institutional repository item page (MINDS@UW, University of Wisconsin) fetched 2026-09-13; no withdrawal or correction notice on the item page. OpenAlex W2902661686 carries no retraction flag.

notes: This is the record R1 finding C-1 identified as decisive and unopened. Its full text was obtained on 2026-09-13 from the institutional repository without authentication (21,237,276 bytes, sha256 81a2a094349a0fccd822247cf2d36b08449bffe2035d30869521049c2dc6a950) and read, including the Methods, Figure 2 and Table 2.

The attribute test was decided from the opened document. The pulley origin height is not stated in the Methods, and Figure 2 depicts a high-to-low path. Under the frozen section 3.2 table the exercise is therefore a related fly-family condition and cannot establish anything about index Y. Absence record A1 survives, but it now survives on a read document rather than on an assumption.

Risk of bias is high for three stated reasons. First, EMG was normalised to the barbell bench press itself rather than to a maximal voluntary contraction, so every value is a ratio to the comparator and no condition has an independent scale. Second, activation was averaged across the concentric and eccentric phases together, so a phase-specific difference cannot be separated. Third, the bodyweight conditions were not load-matched to the 80 per cent of one-repetition maximum used for the loaded conditions, which the thesis itself states.

Grey literature: an MSc thesis is not peer-reviewed. Under the eligibility plan it may inform a tier-4 statement with applicability downgraded, and it may not be the sole support for a published claim.
Surface EMG is an acute activation measure and is not evidence of hypertrophy.

A non-significant difference between the bench press, the peck deck and the cable crossover is not evidence of equivalence. The thesis reports no equivalence margin and n = 14 gives it little power to exclude a moderate difference; the standard deviations (plus or minus 22.0 to 30.5 per cent) are wide relative to the differences.

study.intervention: barbell bench press; bent-forward cable crossovers; peck deck machine; inclined dumbbell flys; seated chest press machine; parallel dips, standard push-ups, suspended push-ups, Swiss ball push-ups
study.population: Subjects were 14 apparently healthy male students aged 19 to 30 years (mean 23, SD 2.8), all with previous resistance-training experience, recruited from the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse.

title: Electromyographical analysis of the pectoralis major muscle during various chest exercises
